Deployment order is fixed: when seeded audits show a single critic's catch-rate below the standing bar on any fall class across two consecutive audits, rubric and context repair MUST execute first; an ensemble MAY deploy only if the repaired single critic still misses on a subsequent audit. All ensemble output is findings only; voting, override, and critic-of-critic structures are prohibited outright. Disagreement between critics is itself a finding class, routed to rulings like any other. Bounds: N ≤ 3 members without an explicit Owner ruling, with cost-per-review telemetry emitted per member, and the ensemble retires on its own kill metric — if its catch-rate gain over the single repaired critic falls under 10 percentage points after one full calibration cycle, it is rent not worth paying.", "resolution": "RECOVERED_FROM_SOURCE_TEXT"}]

## REQ-298 — Rules Service spec::RBM-12

Workbook row: 299 · Authority: PROPOSED · Static delivery disposition: **PARTIAL** · Confidence: medium



> Amendment is a new version through full ceremony; prior version retained, never overwritten



**Intended outcome:** Amending an in-force rule creates a separately identifiable successor through the full applicable ceremony while preserving the prior version and history.

**Gap:** RuleRegistry.append rejects duplicate IDs and remove/replace are denied, but its in-process RuleRecord holds rule_id/source_citation/scope/enforcement_class, with no explicit predecessor/version/history binding. The inspected ceremony append does not establish durable successor lineage and complete tier-ceremony evidence across restart. Append-only methods are a foundation, not the whole amendment promise.

**Required work:** Bind each amendment to a durable prior-version reference and a new version/identity through the existing full tier ceremony, using a ratified additive version envelope where the base RuleRecord is sealed. Retain both immutable versions and their ceremony histories; expose the current effective version without overwriting prior records. Coordinate effective-state atomicity with RBM10.

**Closure demonstration (not executed here):** Amend V1 into V2: early application before required countdown/countersigns refuses; successful ceremony retains queryable V1 and V2 with predecessor and receipts after restart; an attempt to reuse V1 ID with changed content refuses. ## REQ-472 — Pruning & Unlearning Amendment::DAP-37

Workbook row: 473 · Authority: PROPOSED · Static delivery disposition: **PARTIAL** · Confidence: medium



> A fine-tuned artefact MAY be pruned — magnitude pruning or an equivalent structural reduction — between MOAC acceptance and DAP-31's distance gate, as a ruled optional step. Pruning is a second, empirical reduction in memorisation surface on top of DAP-36's differentially private training; it is never a substitute for it, and this document does not present it as one. A pruned artefact MUST re-pass MOAC's acceptance criteria — pruning can degrade performance below the accepted bar, and acceptance is re-evaluated, not assumed to survive the change. A pruned artefact's hash differs from its pre-pruning hash; it is a new artefact for every purpose DAP-10 and DAP-31 govern, including a fresh pass through the distance gate at the ruled threshold. Pruning ratio and method are ruled values, ratified alongside DAP-31's own probe parameters.



**Intended outcome:** DAP-37 corrected with requirement-specific evidence/action and explicit scope limits.

## REQ-473 — Pruning & Unlearning Amendment::DAP-38

Workbook row: 474 · Authority: PROPOSED · Static delivery disposition: **PARTIAL** · Confidence: medium



> When a unit's rights status changes to withdrawn — consent revoked, licence expired, or an equivalent event — every artefact whose training manifest cites that unit is identified via the registry (a query, per RBM-20's design, not a search) and is either re-derived without the unit or recalled. Re-derivation trains a replacement artefact excluding the withdrawn unit, using the same run configuration recorded in the original training manifest, and passes it through DAP-31 and MOAC as a new artefact before it replaces the original in the registry. Recall withdraws the original artefact's registry entry and, where the artefact was already delivered under DAP-10, notifies the receiving party that the artefact's rights basis has changed. A unit's contribution to the estate release budget (DAP-35) is NOT refunded on unlearning — the privacy loss from the original release already occurred; unlearning restores the artefact's cleanliness going forward, not the budget already spent.



**Intended outcome:** DAP-38 corrected with requirement-specific evidence/action and explicit scope limits.

## REQ-474 — serving_integrity_v1::A20.15

Workbook row: 475 · Authority: PROPOSED · Static delivery disposition: **PARTIAL** · Confidence: medium



> A registered artefact MUST be served semantics-stable: identical input, identical seed, identical sampling parameters produce identical output from the identical registered artefact, regardless of memory placement, hardware tier, concurrent load, or storage medium. Resource pressure MAY reduce speed — time-to-first-token, tokens per second — and MUST NOT alter precision, truncate context, substitute a different artefact, or change routing semantics. A serving path that cannot uphold this refuses to serve rather than serving a semantically different model. Verification at load: the serving stack verifies the artefact's hash against the register before the first token. Verification in operation: a token-exact reproduction check against a reference path is runnable on demand and on a standing schedule (cadence: ruled, R-13). A merged-adapter checkpoint is a distinct artefact with its own hash and its own register entry — it passes the gates as itself, on DAP-37's own new-hash precedent.



**Intended outcome:** A20.15 corrected with requirement-specific evidence/action and explicit scope limits.

## REQ-478 — watch_learning_v1::A5.19

Workbook row: 479 · Authority: PROPOSED · Static delivery disposition: **EVIDENCED_SCOPED** · Confidence: high



> Every verdict Grey Mirror passes to Mkono MUST carry a certificate: the set of observed data points that satisfy a ratified certificate requirement (A5.20) for the behaviour asserted, with the requirement's ID and references to the observation records. A certificate contains evidence only. It MUST NOT contain a confidence, score, strength, or probability, and the verdict schema has no field for one — enforced by a signature-as-guard test on CP-S2's precedent. A verdict carrying no certificate is a foundation verdict: it MAY unlock only the reversible ladder — annotate, shape, contain — and severance remains reachable solely from A5.2's registry, unchanged. Mkono's action on a certified verdict is evidenced by that certificate, written to the Ledger with the action. A certificate is legible by construction: it states what was seen, never how worried the detector was.

## REQ-479 — watch_learning_v1::A5.20

## REQ-481 — watch_learning_v1::A5.22

Workbook row: 482 · Authority: PROPOSED · Static delivery disposition: **PARTIAL** · Confidence: medium



> Every unsure case — a verdict with no applicable requirement, or an action routed under AC-4 — enters the research queue with its full observation record. The loop has three roles and one order: CIF proposes what the pattern means — a candidate requirement, or a candidate benign pattern — under its single-experiment principle (BR-9.2: every CIF-originated idea passes a deterministic acceptance point before affecting anything). Solva grounds the proposal — every data point anchored, and a whole-pattern intent audit against the behaviour's objective, which is where the authorised attack that never breaks a rule receives a whole-pattern requirement rather than a per-action one. A human ratifies through RBM-8. The output is a new or amended certificate requirement, or a ratified benign pattern so identical conduct is not re-queued. Research runs outside the hot path; the live case receives graduated response meanwhile, exactly as before.



**Intended outcome:** A5.22 corrected with requirement-specific evidence/action and explicit scope limits.

**Gap:** Static implementation evidence exists for parts of A5.22, but full requirement closure (including governed producer path and scenario proof) is not yet demonstrated in this read-only slice.

**Closure demonstration (not executed here):** Scenario A5.22: execute requirement-specific pass/refusal path and emit immutable receipt evidence; fail on bypass, silent default, or unverifiable branch.

## REQ-596 — security_function_policies_v1::SFP-1

Workbook row: 597 · Authority: PROPOSED · Static delivery disposition: **PARTIAL** · Confidence: medium



> | Assertion Floor | Subjects: any principal requesting a composed answer. Objects: the claim being composed. Operations: assert, compose, refuse. Rule: no sentence enters a composed answer without a per-sentence anchor to material; an unanchorable sentence is refused, not weakened (Doc 4 A2, A5.5). | | **SFP-2** | Certainty-to-Evidence Binding | Subjects: the Watch's response function (Mkono). Objects: severance authority. Operations: unlock, withhold. Rule: severance unlocks only from the closed six-signal registry; no confidence score, however high, is an eligible input (Doc 3 A5.2). | | **SFP-3** | Acceptance Floor | Subjects: any training run. Objects: model output. Operations: accept, refuse. Rule: every stated criterion satisfied or the run is refused in full; no partial acceptance (Promise #22, MOAC). | | **SFP-4** | Custody Floor | Subjects: any data crossing the chokepoint. Objects: the crossing itself. Operations: cross, de-identify, re-identify. Rule: no asset crosses without de-identification appropriate to its custody class (Promise #1, A5.1–A5.3). | | **SFP-5** | Non-Conformance Ceiling | Subjects: any actor whose behavioural signature drifts from its declared conduct. Objects: the actor's trust discount. Operations: reduce, revoke. Rule: loss of conformance alone returns an actor to baseline verification; it is never, by itself, grounds for conviction (Doc 3 A5.7). | | **SFP-6** | Release Budget | Subjects: all external parties, jointly and severally. Objects: the estate's total information release. Operations: release, refuse. Rule: total release across all parties, operations, and time is bounded; exceeding it is a floor violation, not a negotiable ceiling (DAP-35). | | **SFP-7** | Reproduction Ceiling | Subjects: any artefact or output leaving a component boundary. Objects: controlled-unit content. Operations: egress, refuse. Rule: no artefact or output passes carrying reproduction of a controlled unit above the ruled threshold (DAP-31, A5.15). |



**Intended outcome:** SFP-1 corrected with requirement-specific source/code evidence, scoped status, and explicit closure action.
